Tuned Lamborghini Urus in Verde Turbine and Dry Carbon Is Something Else Indeed
13 photos
Photo: Instagram | lartedesign
Even though it is far from being a fresh product anymore, the Lamborghini Urus still makes headlines after all these years. And believe us when we say this, the Italian company’s exotic crossover has started to show its age.
That’s because production started all the way back in 2017 at the Sant’Agata Bolognese facility in Italy (where else?), and five years later, the automaker retired the original Urus, replacing it with the facelifted iteration. The lineup was also expanded to include two members, the Urus Performante and the Urus S, both getting revised looks, some mods beneath the skin, and a power boost from 641 hp (650 ps/478 kW) to 657 hp (666 ps/490 kW).
As you likely recall, the former was a more track-focused version, and was a couple of tenths of a second faster than the latter, despite the fact that both featured the same powertrain in the same configuration. The Raging Bull then expanded the lineup with the Urus SE , the first-ever plug-in hybrid version of the high-riding model. The electrified 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged V8 engine was officially rated at 789 hp (800 ps/589 kW) and 710 lb-ft (950 Nm) of torque, and 0-62 mph (100 kph) took 3.4 seconds.
But why do we speak about this model in past tense when it came out two years ago? Because that’s how long it lived before the automaker pulled the plug on it. The sole surviving member of the Urus lineup is the new Urus SE Performante. This model has dropped the sprint time to 3.3 seconds, identical to yesterday’s non-electrified Performante, and has 801 hp (812 ps/597 kW) and 738 lb-ft (1,000 Nm) of torque in total available via the right pedal, produced by its upgraded PHEV powertrain.
Photo: Instagram | lartedesign Now, the Lamborghini Urus SE may be dead and buried, but it is the model that has started getting the most coverage in our news feed. That’s because quite a few tuners have dropped all kinds of modded takes on it these past few weeks and months, and Larte Design’s name is definitely toward the top of the list. One of their latest projects based on this model can be seen in the photo gallery, and it definitely looks quite memorable, especially if you are into tuned examples.
In our (or my, in this case) opinion, one of the first things that makes it stand out from a crowd is the Verde Turbine matte paint finish, and the exposed dry carbon elements. The former is the color that dominates the entire exterior of this tuned Lamborghini Urus SE, and the latter can be seen on some of the add-ons. The latter include the new splitter with blades on the sides, the fresh side skirts, the wheels arch trim, and some extras in the front bumper.
This modded Italian exotic crossover also benefits from a quite large diffuser at the rear, which features the ever-present extra brake light. Or two of them, in this case. The tailpipe trim appears to be new as well, and further up, it sports a ducktail spoiler above the taillights, as well as a new roof-mounted wing. Are the Y-spoke alloys, shod in Pirelli P Zero tires, part of the makeover, too? Your guess is as good as ours, and since we’re not exactly wheel experts, we will leave this answer to you.
Photo: Instagram | lartedesign Do you want to see the interior of this modded Lamborghini Urus SE? Well, so do we, but unfortunately, Larte Design hasn’t released any images of it at the time of writing. And you know what this usually means, don’t you? With an emphasis on the word “usually,” that would be that the vehicle in question probably retains its stock upholstery, trim, and so on.
There is also no word on power, and chances are that this machine might not offer any more oomph, and that would be all right, as the model is already very punchy with no mods.
There is no detail on the pricing part of the extras mentioned above either, which fit the 2025 to 2027 model year Lamborghini Urus SE , though the money part shouldn’t be an issue to owners, given that a used Urus SE tends to retail from $270,000 to over $350,000 in today’s used car market in the United States of America, based on the model year, mileage, options, and overall appearance.
Nevertheless, Larte Design invites interested parties to reach out to them and discuss the details, so your Lamborghini Urus SE could also look like this. But the question is, would you want it to? If you said yes, and you have a Urus SE parked in your garage, then congrats, and you may want to contact the tuner for the next part. Before wrapping it up and moving on to the next topic, let us know if you fancy the look of this tuned example by dropping a few lines below. Most Compact and Versatile: A Family or Couple-Ready Toy Hauler at Just 10 Feet Is Possible
31 photos
Photo: 7even50 Camper
The smaller a camper the harder it is to integrate as much versatility into it as possible. However, some crews manage to hit the sweet spot in terms in capability and a compact profile. One team that achieves this balance is 7even50.
It’s here that we find the Biker & Family (BF), a travel trailer that, upon my first impression, left me wanting to dive in deeper to really see what it can do. Its size first grabbed my attention, and soon after, the interior and entire unit as a whole. It’s that good.
Now, what we’re looking at here may just be one of, if not, the most versatile little box with wheels that I’ve encountered this year. I say this because, one, our team runs across countless campers on a daily basis, so we see quite a few and have the knowledge base necessary to compare and contrast RVs from all over the world, and two, well, read on.
Photo: 7even50 Camper The BF is a camper that, despite its size, can be adapted to serve the lifestyle needs of lone travelers, families, and even those of us that have a couple of e-bikes, kayaks, or other gear with which you let loose in the wilderness. But, you can also stuff a dirt bike or smaller motorcycle into a BF.
Yes, it can also be a toy hauler, and all you need is a wheel choke at the front, and in my personal opinion, a strap with rachet or two. Come to think of it, some BF units that 7even50 have completed for owners include a bicycle rack on the trailer nosecone, meaning we can bring all that I mentioned above, and all at once; just throw the kayak on top; they’re typically light and won’t damage a handlebar or motorcycle seat by laying on top. You get the idea here.
Best of all, once you finally make it to wherever your map leads, you can unload the interior, hide the straps and all that, wipe the tire marks off the floor, if there are any, and after setting up the table and fluffing up your pillows, you’re looking at a home away from home.
Sure, all this sounds very normal for a toy hauler, but not forget to consider just how small this trailer is. It’s 3.04 m (10ft, box dimensions), and 1.51 m (5 ft) wide. Height stands at 1.5 m (4.9 ft), so moving around inside will be done with a slouch.
Photo: 7even50 Camper While this does come across as a downside, it does push us to spend as much time outdoors as possible, reserving the interior for sleeping, lounging on a cool morning as you wait for the dew to dry up, or reading a book on a rainy day. We can toss dining into the mix, but only on some occasions since the whole idea is to hang around outside.
Interiors aren’t all that complicated either, with the front end of the BF used for a storage system that also creates a countertop for some of your knick-knacks, and as we move toward the rear, the drive side is occupied by half of the bedding platform during day-to-day living with tables along the camping side. This is good for work and some chit-chats.
Come nighttime, this area turns into a complete wall-to-wall bed that can easily be suitable for two adults and a child. It’s completed with the help of a rail and ledge along the right wall. Some models include a solid block instead of a drop-down ledge, just in case you need the system to handle a bit more weight. This also tells me that 7even50 works with future owners to give them the camper they want and need.
Photo: 7even50 Camper During day mode, the couch has ample storage underneath, and during the evening, the raised platform continues to provide storage space underneath. If I may, this feature is bound to be used in some rounds of hide and seek.
Keep in mind that the space can also be adapted to create a U-shaped dinette that does appear to be suitable for a group of three to four guests playing a game of cards. I like this level of versatility and even the way the seating forces you to stay out once you’re locked in, to an extent. There are just so many ways you can sit around in here.
The last area in the BF is located by the door, where a little galley block is in place which doesn’t offer much except some cabinets, a tiny countertop, and a fridge on a slideout. Luckily, 7even50 did craft the rear of the BF for a tent annex, so you can easily expand and complete the kitchen outside.
While this is the point where I’d normally bring an introduction into a camper to a close, the BF demands even more attention, especially outside.
Photo: 7even50 Camper What I found rather neat about what 7even50 has done with the place, so to speak, is that they’ve made the unit suitable for roof-top mounted gear, so that kayak I mentioned, doesn’t even need to end up inside. But, a roof-rack also means that an RTT can be added, expanding sleeping capacity to as much as the tent allows. Keep in mind, however, that there’s a limit of 300 kg (661 lbs static) for the roof load.
But, that’s not all we can call upon. The shell can also call upon a rack system that allows us to mount spare tires, gas cans, shovels, recovery boards, ropes, you name it, further expanding this camper’s versatility. Our off-road adventures are, on the other hand, limited by the axle suspension, which also means a GVWR of 1,300 kg (2,866 lbs), of which, around 500-600 kg (1,102-1,322 lbs) is for cargo.
Photo: 7even50 Camper This brings us to price. According to the manufacturer’s website, a standard Biker & Family starts off at €18,974, or roughly $20,800, but be sure to calculate taxes and fees and any other options you add to the mix.
What I must point out is that 7even50 is a German team, and US and North American residents will have a hard time bringing this one over to the US. It’s not impossible, but is costly. Better yet, look for something similar in the US, which is going to be a bit of a hurdle, but there are some options out here too.
A couple you can look into is the inTech Flyer Explore and ROG lineup from Encore RV. Until next time.

How Much Does a 2023 Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing Cost After 24,254 Miles?
11 photos
Photo: Instagram | jesus.spec
Does the rather aging Cadillac CT5 still keep you up at night? Well, we won’t blame you if it does, because this thing looks a lot better than most of the premium mid-size models on sale today.
Things get a lot more exciting if you consider sprucing up your life with the Blackwing model, because this one is a veritable BMW M5 fighter. Everyone and their pet knows that it features an LT4 V8 engine. The supercharged mill has a 6.2-liter displacement, and pumps out no less than 668 brake horsepower (498 kW/678 ps) and 659 lb-ft (893 Nm) of torque.
That’s without anyone tampering with its engine, which can be paired either with a six-speed manual transmission or an available ten-speed automatic unit. Cadillac’s CT5-V Blackwing takes just 3.4 seconds to sprint from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph), and that’s actually quicker than the iconic Ferrari Enzo, and flat-out, it will do over 200 mph or 322+ kph.
Pictured in the gallery is a 2023 model year that features the stick shift. The business super sedan in question has a white look, some glossy black details, and rides on dark gray wheels. It also sports tinted windows, and the interior mixes white and black leather upholstery, sprinkled with red piping, some red stitching, red seatbelts, black pillars, and a black headliner, among other things.
Photo: Instagram | jesus.spec Some carbon fiber trim is also on deck here, there is a red 12 o’clock marker on the steering wheel, and as we told you above, it is a stick shift machine . The pictures released by the selling dealer do not allow us to see whether there is any wear on the driver’s seat, but there should be some, given that this is a 2023 model year car, which had 25,254 miles (40,642 km) under its belt at the time of cataloging.
Now, just because it is a used example does not mean that it will go easy on your wallet, as the average Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing that hits the used car market in the United States of America tends to sell from roughly $80,000 to over $125,000. It all depends on the model year, mileage, options, overall conditions, and so on. The 2026 MY starts at $98,900 (MSRP), and in case you forgot, the CT5 production is ending at the end of 2026.
But how much do you think this 2023 Cadillac CT5-V Blackwing costs? Unless you said $94,995, then you are wrong, because this was the asking price at the time of writing. The car in question is advertised on social media by @jesus.spec, which invites interested parties to reach out to them for more information. So, could this be your next used cool ride? 15 New Tarmac Works Collectibles You Can Buy Today
44 photos
Photo: Tarmac Works
I’m facing a “huge” dilemma. You could say it’s a first-world problem, as I realize it’s not something most people would be concerned about. I’m working with a designer to find the best solution for my new office/man cave. It’s not a huge room, and I want it to integrate three of my hobbies plus the work side of things.
I’ve mentioned I want some sort of display for my motorcycle helmets, racing memorabilia, and diecast collectibles. I’ve been thinking about those wall-mounted display cases as an option, and I’m starting to think I should keep brands separate. Hot Wheels and Matchbox would be on one side, Mini GT and Kaido House on another, then there’s the Tarmac Works area, but what about my Kyosho, Tomica and Solido cars?
It’s even more complicated with the latter as they’re all 1/18th-scale models. I could make things simple and just keep 50 collectibles total and organize them by theme: JDM, Drifting, Racing, Supercars or something along those lines. Right now I’m almost buried in tiny cars, as I’ve been actively ordering dozens of them again.
I’m currently trying to bring my Mini GT line-up up to par with the Tarmac Works models I’ve unboxed this year. And there’s this voice inside my head that keeps pushing me to join the TW Owners Club, if only to get access to the TWOC Members Only Models (a minimum of two per year). The final November pre-order went live about a week ago, and I signed up for both of the two Ferraris.
However, if you need some new cars to enjoy before Christmas, the November release features a line-up of 15 vehicles to choose from. The Porsche 911 GT3 R is the largest of them all, as it’s a 1/43rd-scale item. It’s also the most expensive one here at $46.90 before taxes. I believe it had a MoonEyes themed livery the first time we saw it, too, and I prefer that black and yellow look over the new version.
There’s a new 1/43rd-scale Porsche in town! Photo: Tarmac Works This thing reportedly weighs 1.1 lbs/0.5 kg, and that makes me curious to see how it compares to Mattel’s Premium 1/43rd-scale models. I’m quite excited to see the Vertex Toyota Aristo JZS161, mainly because it’s an HKS/Taniguchi special model. This casting was just recently available as a MOM release for $12.90. Production was limited to 768 units, and there’s even a Chrome Chase version to look for if you’re interested in that sort of thing.
I’m doing my best to expand my D1GP collection, and Tarmac Works has been an incredible source for that in recent years. And the latest drop is solid proof for that, as the URAS Skyline ER34 is making its debut in the Global64 series. Uras is basically “Monkey” spelled backwards in Japanese, and you might remember how silly Ken Nomura used to act during D1GP events.
It’s safe to assume some of the iconic liveries he used over the years will make their way into the 1/64th-scale Universe thanks to Felix and his team in Hong Kong. The First Edition of the ER34 casting still looks great in plain blue, and this time I’m curious to get a closer look at the Chrome Blue chase. You can also opt for the blister version of the collectible if you enjoy displaying it that way.
Speaking of Nissan Skylines , the John Sibal-designed, widebody R32 is now available with a new look. It’s another artistic project in collaboration with Sean Wotherspoon, which reminds me of the Hot Wheels Deora Mattel released not long ago. I unboxed both the Millennium Jade and Greddy variations of the casting in June this year and it is without doubt one of the nicer R32s you can find on the market. Still, because of this iteration’s special nature, it can cost between $19.90 and $36.90 before tax.
Chase model takes a different route Photo: Tarmac Works I would rather go after something else within that same budget instead. For the Porsche 928 S you can also opt between the regular packaging and the blister card which is nice. The reason why there are two cars in some of the presentation photos might not be so obvious, as it’s a game of “spot the differences”. Look at the headlights!
The one with the pop-up headlights is the Chase version, so there’s no livery change here. I think it’s a fairly creative way of doing things, even though some people might not enjoy it as much. The funny part is that I believe the original, First Edition of the casting had it the other way around. That car featured a simple, red paint job, and it also lacked the Safety Car lights we now have on this iteration.
It’s the kind of flexibility you’ll often see at Tarmac Works and it makes collecting these cars all the more enjoyable. The Ford Mustang GTD has been out for a few years now and it makes perfect sense that multiple scale model car manufacturers have created replicas of it. You can’t expect a $2 Hot Wheels to look like a $11.90 version of the American machine from Tarmac Works though. It’s part of the Global64 series, where you’ll also find the Shelby GT350R/GT4.
I believe this is just the second iteration of the casting, as the previous one was red with black stripes down the middle. One of my local dealers has a 25% discount for it, which says a lot about how popular the model was where I live. This dealer almost never comes up with discounts this big. Now, TW’s Hobby64 line is slightly more expensive to get into, but I think it’s worth going for it if you want the coolest models possible for your collection.
DTM fans rejoice! Photo: Tarmac Works The new variation of the Audi R8 LMS GT3 evo II is a throwback to UNO Racing’s 24h of Spa challenge from 2023. The R8 has to be one of the most popular cars for the Hong Kong-based manufacturer, as you’ll find around 60 variations of it across multiple castings.
While you can only buy a maximum of three units of the UNO Racing Special Edition in pink (at $23.90 each), there’s no limit to how many replicas of the FIA GT World Cup 2025 you can get.
At $36.90 each, expect to find some Tarmac Cards inside as well. I’ve unboxed a few myself this year, but it’s not a direction I’m keen on pursuing for the future. Porsches are just as popular in the Tarmac Works Universe, and I’m not just talking about RWB collectibles. There are three different castings for the 911 GT3 R, starting with the older ones all the way up to the 992.
You’ll find a Falken-powered one in each category, and for the latest drop we’re looking at the #33 car which I saw live at last year’s 24H Nurburgring event . Neither one of the team’s cars managed to finish the race sadly, but this is still an iconic machine nonetheless. If you must have something with a proven record behind it, I’m sure Ayhancan Güven’s DTM winner will satisfy that need.
Takumi switched to a Mercedes? Photo: Tarmac Works As much as I love Initial D, seeing the black and white livery on a Mercedes-AMG GT3 does nothing for me and I’ll easily skip both the Bathurst 12h 2026 and the Shanghai 8 Hours variations.
The Jever Racing livery is a bit more exciting on a Porsche 911 GT1 than it is on an Audi A4, but I’d still buy the latter if only for all the years I spent driving Audis around Europe for motorsports events.
Also, this reminds me that the 911 GT1 is part of TW’s Hobby64+ series, which currently only features three castings (Ford RS200 and Lancia 037 Rally). The Toy Story LB-KAIDO WORKS R32 Skyline is another item I will ignore, and I wonder if I can ever feel that way about the F40 GT.
It’s not even my favorite Ferrari ever, and I would still happily hunt for every one of the seven other variations on the market (plus the GTE!). You see, we’re really living in a golden age for collecting diecast models!

Avatr T09 Debuts With 1,000+ Horsepower and Rolls-Royce Looks at a Fraction of the Price
11 photos
Photo: Avatr Technology
The Avatr T09 has officially debuted at the 2026 Guangzhou Auto Show as a 5.3-meter flagship luxury SUV backed by Changan, Huawei, and CATL, ahead of a December market launch. Available with up to 1,000 horsepower and over 240 miles of electric range, it features imposing, Rolls-Royce-inspired proportions and a triple-screen HarmonySpace 5 cabin.
If a Rolls-Royce Cullinan ultra-luxury SUV and a Land Rover Range Rover Long Wheelbase had a baby, it would probably look just like the new Avatr T09. However, at nearly 5.3 meters long, there is nothing "baby" about its massive proportions.
The SUV is 208.1 inches (5,285 millimeters) long, 79.7 inches (2,025 millimeters) wide, and 71.3 inches (1,810 millimeters) tall, sitting on a wheelbase of 124.0 inches (3,150 millimeters). The numbers position the Avatr T09 right between its "parents."
It is longer than a Range Rover Long Wheelbase and just two inches shy of a Rolls-Royce Cullinan, while offering far more horsepower and tech in its range-topping form than both of them at a fraction of the price. Because that is what the Chinese car industry does.
Photo: ChinaCarNews | Autohome Penned at the Avatr Global Design Center in Munich by a team led by former BMW designer Nader Faghihzadeh, the T09 evolves from the brand's own Vision Xpectra concept. The made-in-China SUV features an upright grille with 362 illuminated Avatr logo elements and million-pixel smart projection headlights. Its tall, boxy silhouette with squared-off fenders mirrors full-size luxury land yachts like the Rolls-Royce Cullinan.
In the meantime, optional two-tone body paint schemes, splitting the upper section from the lower body, and heavy chrome trim along the doors and D-pillars are a clear indication that this SUV wants a piece of the market share currently shared by the Mercedes-Maybach GLS, Bentley Bentayga , and Rolls-Royce Cullinan.
The six-seat cabin hosts the 10.25-inch instrument cluster and dual 17.2-inch screens for the center console and front passenger, running HarmonySpace 5. And now comes the fun part. The model features the Vortex. When you start the car, a quiet motor raises it out of the dashboard, and it retracts flush when you shut the vehicle off, complete with an anti-pinch sensor so it won’t catch your fingers.
The sculpture is made from natural wood and a translucent smoky-gray glass, and it is not just for show (or show-off, because you know the Chinese!). It integrates 118 individually controlled LEDs that sync with the rest of the cabin’s ambient lighting to act as a visual assistant.
Photo: Avatr Technology When you talk to Huawei’s voice assistant, the lights pulse and ripple like a physical “face,” taken right out of a sci-fi movie. This way, you know that the car is listening and responding. It also sends safety alerts, flashing various warnings. For instance, it pulses red and amber if a car or cyclist is approaching rapidly from behind while you are parked.
The six-seat cabin offers 19.4 cubic feet (550 liters) of cargo space, with the third-row seats in use. When necessary, the seats in the third row can fold flat into the floor in just 18 seconds, at the push of a button, to make more luggage room in no time.
The lineup starts with the 1.5-liter dual-motor all-wheel-drive Avatr T09, which pairs the 1.5-liter turbocharged inline-four with two electric motors, one mounted on the front axle and another out back, for a combined output of 657 horsepower (666 metric horsepower).
At the top of the range sits the variant powered by a 2.0-liter turbocharged inline-four, working alongside three electric motors, with one sitting up front and two more driving the rear wheels. The setup is estimated to pump out an incredible 1,000 horsepower (1,014 metric horsepower), but the official numbers have yet to be confirmed.
Photo: ChinaCarNews | Autohome The Cullinan -wannabe is equipped with a 71.24 kWh CATL Xiaoyao battery pack, which stores enough energy for a drive of up to 249 miles (400 kilometers) on electric power only, in the very generous CLTC standard. The stricter WLTC cycle rates it between 186 and 205 miles (300 to 330 kilometers), depending on the powertrain.
The Avatr T09 is built around a Taihang Smart Control Chassis, which integrates Huawei XMC 3.0 and dual-chamber air suspension. Rear-wheel steering with up to 10 degrees of angle gives the 208.1-inch SUV a tight turning radius of only 15.26 feet (4.65 meters). The T09 debuts Huawei Qiankun ADS 5 supported by a quad-LiDAR sensor array, including an 896-line roof-mounted main radar.
The model is expected to start at around 500,000 yuan, which translates to roughly $74,600. The automaker will reveal the exact pricing in December, when the SUV’s market launch is scheduled to take place. The Avatr T09, designed in Munich, will roll off the production line of Changan Automobile's smart factory in Chongqing, China.
The Avatr T09 was previewed by a concept car unveiled at the Paris Motor Show back in October, which is a clear sign that the model is preparing for a European debut. Norway and Spain are the first countries set to receive it next year. Australia is slated to receive right-hand-drive versions in 2028, while Middle Eastern markets are also on the export roadmap.

BamBuk's Tip-Proof Tandem E-Trike Brings New Freedom to Those With Limited Physical Abilities
15 photos
Photo: BamBuk
Cycling has typically always been a single-occupant activity, at least, if you’re not riding in a group. However, over the years, tandem bicycles made their appearance, unlocking rides on two wheels with multiple occupants on the same frame.
Tandem bicycles are those rides you see out there upon which two or more riders share the same frame and ride dynamics , at least, in its simplest form. There are also some wild tandems that explore the presence of more than just two people, with the world record holder rolling in with a length of 117 ft and 5 in, and capable of handling as many people as will fit; it’s basically like a warehouse support beam.
Photo: BamBuk As the years rolled by and we’ve exhausted bicycle frame styles and abilities, at least, at first sight, we’ve begun to mix and match, almost crossbreed cycling disciplines, giving rise to new variations. Toss in the electrification of our world, and cycling design and capabilities have simply snowballed into the sort of creatures we see these days.
This brings us to the option we have before us today, a recumbent tandem bike that is also electrified to assist us in moving around town with a load that’s double what we normally experience on a bicycle. Sure, the second pedaling system will help split the work, but having electric assistance just takes the whole thing to a new level of ease-of-use.
Now, the tandem e-tricycle from BamBuk, the centerpiece of our discussion today, is one of those cycling options that frankly, upon seeing it for the first time, inspired me to complete this article, and there are countless reasons why you explore further.
Photo: BamBuk First and foremost, as a tandem option, you and a loved one can hop on and get that blood flowing, together. That alone means afternoon rides of a different vibe, ones where we smile and tell jokes as the landscape progresses.
Secondly, it means a vehicle and an activity that’s accessible to as many people as possible, and in various stages of health. Due to the electric assistance, the BamBuk e-trike means that it can be used by persons with limited mobility, strength, and various ages.
This brings us back to the first benefit, and one of the scenarios that I imagined the moment I locked eyes with this urban mobility solution. As we age, we can’t deny that the body starts to break down, and my parents and I are no exception from the rule.
So, I saw the BamBuk as a wonderful solution to take my mom out for a ride, sharing laughs and bonding along the way, and with electric assistance ensuring that she can manage the ride, even with some of the health issues her body is subject to.
Photo: BamBuk Considering that a 5th generation Bosch CX motor is in place on the BamBuk, capable of producing a whopping 120 Nm of torque, so even with limited strength, there’s ample assistance to move both people with ease.
As you’d expect, this power is drawn from a battery pack, and Bosch continues to supply the spunk. With a 545 Wh battery, BamBuk mentions a peak ride time of up to 70 km (44 miles), but we can also add another pack, so doubling range to as much as 140 km (88 miles). That’s ample juice even if you encounter hills while two people are enjoying the ride.
Overall, the BamBuk is typically sold in one style , but that frame can be equipped with a wide range of features and equipment, in the process, creating three different trim levels that start off at as much as €10,462 ($11,450) and as high as €15,638 ($17,100), as much as some used cars, even some new ones.
Be sure to explore each trim level to see what it brings to the table. But, as an idea of what to expect, think Rohloff gearboxes, freewheel for the rear rider, quad-piston brakes, and adjustability you won’t believe.
Photo: BamBuk One of the coolest tricks of the BamBuk e-trikes is that they have an adjustable frame that we can collapse to reduce its length to as little as 2 meters (6.5 ft), allowing us to toss it on the rear of an RV or camper and exploring the wildest of places. It’s a trick that not very many, if any, tandem trikes can achieve.
Last but not least, Bambuk mentions that they’ve taken things to the next level, having developed a tip-proof trike, and the way they do it is with the suspension system integrated into the trikes. Each wheel is supported by an independent system, and the frame flexes a bit when the front and rear take hits at different times.
Sure, the BamBuk e-trike is one hella expensive mobility solution, but if you think about the level of bonding and mobility that this solution can bring back into your life is not to be overlooked, especially if someone in the family is subject to limited strength and health.

Koenigsegg Jesko Terrang Is a Virtual Take on the Sterrato & 911 Dakar From a Hypercar Perspective
24 photos
Photo: abimelecdesign / Instagram
Abimelec Arellano, a virtual artist better known as " abimelecdesign " on social media, has prepared the newest wishful-thinking project - a crazy supercar. The member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators stopped dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular design at the behest of a news outlet.
The good folks over at Motor1 came up with a wacky idea – “What if Koenigsegg built an off-road supercar to rival the Lamborghini Huracan Sterrato and Porsche 911 Dakar?” The Swedish automaker, an exotic company focused mainly on hypercars, is currently focused on a different thing - Christian von Koenigsegg took note of the recent BYD electric supercar top speed record and said that his brand still wants to push for a record-breaking run with the Jesko Absolut.
The latter theoretically can reach up to 330 mph, which is 532 kph, but it’s much harder to put it into practice: there are no tires capable of withstanding such extreme speeds. Just recently, BYD’s luxury brand Yangwang announced that its U9 Xtreme reached 312.65 mph (503.17 kph) on November 1.
The first production car that soared above the 310-mph (500-kph) threshold was officially recognized by the FIA, and the Chinese electric hypercar also has two Guinness World Records now, so it’s understandable why von Koenigsegg suddenly remembered their Jesko Absolut might be capable of more. Additionally, they now also have the financial means to pursue the record.
Also, recently Koenigsegg gained a new investment from a private equity firm, with the company now valued at around €1.3 billion ($1.4 billion at the current exchange rate). That also means they might be open to developing new versions – which is probably why the news outlet allied with the pixel master to imagine a potential new Jesko variant.
Dubbed the Terrang, it goes in a different direction – a mild off-road version that gives up some of the supercar prowess for a bit of “extra ground clearance and all-terrain capability.” They imagined the new version with a raised ride height, meaty off-road tires, and extra cladding for the lower parts of the body. However, the power setup would remain the same – 5.0-liter twin-turbo V8 with 1,280 hp or 1,600 hp on E85, just tuned for better low-rpm torque response.
Given the tremendous popularity of the Lamborghini Huracan Sterrato and Porsche 911 Dakar special editions, we shouldn’t exclude the possibility of more automakers going down that route – though nobody can tell for sure if Koenigsegg would be up for the task in the real world. So, what do you think – yay or nay? Or maybe they should just throw us a full-size SUV directly, just like McLaren is preparing to do? The Hyundai Stellar Four-Door Sedan Is a Virtual Proposal For a Very Different Kind of Aesthetics
9 photos
Photo: sshshhhhhh / Instagram
The good folks over at Hyundai are currently kicking off the latest design revolution dubbed ‘Art of Steel’ with major local and international models like the Avante, Bayon, or the best-selling Tucson, of course.
Alongside Kia, Hyundai has never been afraid to experiment – and the South Korean automaker has grown tremendously to the point of announcing one yearly sales record after another in major regions like the United States. From a little-known Asian carmaker to a global powerhouse was a long road, and the company traveled it with poise and confidence – especially in recent years.
As such, nobody is now surprised that Hyundai dares to innovate once again – they have proven to be a powerhouse in terms of EVs and even as a premium manufacturers through the Genesis brand subsidiary. This summer, at home in South Korea, they kicked off the new ‘ Art of Steel ’ design language together with the eighth-generation Hyundai Avante and Tucson.
The former was launched in June 2026 at the Busan International Mobility Show, and the latter, now reaching its fifth iteration (NX5), was first announced in August. The Hyundai Tucson reached international stardom at the 2026 Paris Motor Show in October when it was revealed in European specification alongside the smaller Hyundai Bayon, which is also following in its footsteps.
The fall automotive season continued for Hyundai with the launch of the international Elantra in November at the 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show (AutoMobility LA), with the 2027 Elantra and the 2028 Elantra Hybrid, seconded by the debuts in America of the all-new Tucson and Palisade XRT Pro alongside the brand-new Genesis G80 and GV80 Hybrid models.
Most likely, Hyundai will continue to showcase new models featuring the Art of Steel design language, although there was also some bad news – like the retirement of the larger Hyundai Sonata from the Australian market, where the new i30 Sedan (aka Elantra) will take its place. By the way, the Sonata is the largest sedan currently available in America, where it’s sold along with the compact Elantra.
Hyundai, on the other hand, has a gap in the lineup in terms of large passenger cars – they want you to go to Genesis to buy the larger sedans or jump into their crossover SUV lineup. Well, not everyone wants that – and just recently a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators found a solution to the predicament.
More precisely, the South Korean virtual artist Shin Sung-hwan, better known as ' sshshhhhhh ' on social media, has already cooked up Hyundai's potential next design language after 'Art of Steel' in their unofficial, hypothetical design project – and they also showcase a large sedan alongside it. Dubbed Hyundai Stellar, just like the model from 1983 to 1992, this is a minimalist, retro-modern four-door sedan model packing what look like recycled bumpers and rail-style front and rear LED lighting elements.
It also comes with an angular profile and massive alloy wheels, as well as classic four-door proportions and what looks like a leather-appointed interior. Quite obviously, if it ever existed, this model would place above the current Sonata. As for the powertrain, there are no obvious hints, which means it could be ICE, electrified, or a full EV.
So, what do you think? Should Hyundai think about building something like this – considering there’s a massive gap in the market in America when it comes to large sedans? Would this model represent a good alternative to the costlier German executive sedans or to the Dodge Charger sedan, for example? View this post on Instagram A post shared by 신성환 (@sshshhhhhh)

Hackers Now Target Mechanics, Repair Shops With Infected Vehicle Diagnostic Software
7 photos
Photo: Bogdan Popa/autoevolution
A new malicious campaign that was spotted on no more, no less than 16 fake GitHub repositories is specifically aimed at repair shops and technicians looking for vehicle diagnostic software online.
Research conducted by automotive cybersecurity company Upstream revealed a clever approach to a rather traditional method of infecting computers.
Instead of distributing malicious files, which would be blocked by antivirus software, the fake GitHub repositories actually include “legitimate open-source code, including standard CAN database (.dbc) files, ISO-TP transport helpers, and UDS service classes,” as the security firm explains.
The whole trick is simple: the hackers hope to convince users, most often technicians whose laptops are connected to dealer portals, therefore benefit from access to the networks operated by automakers, to download the packages. Once they extract the files, they are instructed to download additional payloads.
To do this, they are being told “to run local package installers, like editable pip commands, or compile solution files,” the security firm notes.
All packages come with attached README files that include all the instructions and lengthy descriptions to make the files look genuine. The documents are created using artificial intelligence and specifically use automotive-specific phrases, especially to appear in Google searches and, therefore, find more targets.
Photo: Genesis This isn’t the only mechanism used by hackers to convince technicians to install the infected files. A 404.html file, typically used to display an error when no page is found, is included in the root directory with a very simple, yet quite clever role. It displays a GitHub loading package message and a progress bar, but in the background, it connects to a remote server to redirect the browser.
“When victims click the repository’s associated GitHub Pages link or open the file locally, they are routed to external infrastructure that probably hosts credential-stealing payloads,” the cybersecurity firm explains.
In case you wonder what happens when all these steps are executed and a computer is infected, it all comes down to the information the bad actors can steal and eventually monetize or use for other malicious purposes.
Service technicians and repair shops use laptops to connect to our vehicles and obtain vehicle diagnostics data that allow them to read fault codes and figure out what’s wrong with a car. In some cases, the software they use communicates with the portals operated by automakers, and these laptops are configured to automatically log in and access their networks.
Photo: Genesis Once they access the portal, service technicians can access additional data to help with the repairs, get codes for the needed vehicle parts, and request additional files if software updates – such as for the infotainment unit – are needed.
This is precisely the point attackers hope to reach as part of this sophisticated attempt.
“Workshop computers routinely store cached single sign-on (SSO) tokens, active browser cookies for OEM service portals, saved credentials for telematics aggregators, and local certificates tied to J2534 interfaces,” the security firm explains.
“If a suspected infostealer exfiltrates those session tokens, attackers can inject them into their own browsers to hijack authenticated sessions, potentially bypassing multi-factor authentication and logging directly into OEM dealer portals to expose VIN histories, warranty systems, and connected-vehicle infrastructure.”
GitHub projects are specifically sought-after in the automotive world not only by vehicle owners but also by service technicians who are continuously looking into new ways to conduct certain operations. For example, one of the most recent projects gaining particular attention in the automotive space is a method to enable Google Maps and Waze on the digital cockpit in vehicles part of the Volkswagen Group.
Photo: Genesis The method works on MIB2-powered units and is extensively documented in numerous GitHub projects, where technicians can find step-by-step instructions to install the software in certain vehicles. The process involves downloading certain packages and compiling them locally before loading them on a compatible vehicle through the USB port.
The unlocking requires approximately 45 minutes to complete, after which users can run navigation apps directly on their digital cockpits, while the main infotainment screen can still be used for running CarPlay. All these GitHub pages have become very popular in the last few weeks.
The cybersecurity firm claims this malicious campaign has been observed since the first days of November, and it will likely continue by the end of the year and into early 2027.
The cybersecurity company recommends that additional protection methods be employed to prevent computers that had previously been infected from accessing and extracting certain data. “Harden dealer portals with strict token binding, anomaly detection, and shorter session lifetimes to reduce the impact of stolen cookies,” the security company explains in its blog post.
The good news is that the GitHub pages discovered to be used as part of this campaign have already been removed, but security researchers warn that more such attempts might appear in the near future, so paying close attention to the payloads you are prompted to download is critical.
